title: CHAPTER 7: TEMPLES, HERITAGE SITES AND TOURISM

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Pancharamas are five sacred Shiva temples in Andhra Pradesh: Amararama, Somarama, Kshararama, Bhimarama, and Kumararama.
UNESCO World Heritage Sites possess exceptional cultural or natural importance requiring global preservation.
South Indian temple architecture predominantly showcases the Dravidian style with monumental Gopurams and detailed Vimanas.
Heritage sites reflect the patron dynasties such as the Chalukyas, Cholas, Vijayanagara, and Kakatiyas.

blocks.content: Pancharamas represent five sacred ancient shrines of Lord Shiva situated across Andhra Pradesh.

cells: Tirumala Hills, Tirupati (Chittoor); dedicated to Lord Venkateswara (Vishnu); richest Hindu temple in the world by income and second most visited religious site globally; annual 'Brahmotsavam' festival draws millions
Kurnool; Mallikarjuna Swamy – one of 12 Jyotirlingas; located on Krishna River gorge; also dedicated to Bhramaramba Devi (one of 18 Shakti Peethas)
Guntur (near Amaravati); ancient Buddhist stupa; 2nd century BCE; one of largest Buddhist monuments in India; closely related to Nagarjunakonda
Guntur / Nalgonda border area (on island in Nagarjunasagar reservoir); one of the world's greatest Buddhist centers; excavated stupas, viharas; museum on the island
Vijayawada (Indrakeeladri hill on Krishna River); the presiding deity of Vijayawada; major Navratri festival draws hundreds of thousands
Visakhapatnam (Simhachalam Hill); dedicated to Narasimha Swamy (Varaha-Lakshmi Narasimha); famous for 'Chandana Yatra'
Bhadradri Kothagudem (now in Telangana, but historically significant to AP); Lord Sri Sitaramachandra Swamy; famous Rama Navami celebration
East Godavari; one of Pancharamas (5 Shiva temples in AP/Telangana); important Shaiva center
Chittoor (near Tirupati); one of Pancha Bhuta Stalas (Air element); Rahu-Ketu puja famous
East Godavari; one of five Pancharamas; location differs – combined counting
Guntur; rock-cut caves; 4th-5th century CE; one of the earliest rock-cut temples in Andhra
Anantapur; Veerabhadra temple; famous for Nandi Statue (world's largest monolithic Nandi) and hanging pillar; Vijayanagara architecture
Anantapur; Sri Satya Sai Baba Ashram; international pilgrim center
Krishna River at Vijayawada; Bhavani Island (world's largest inhabited river island?)
Visakhapatnam; picturesque tribal hill station; coffee plantations; Borra Caves (stalactite/stalagmite caves)
Ramakrishna Beach, Beach Road – major tourist attractions
East Godavari; scenic river gorge; boat journey on Godavari between Papikondalu hills

rows: Built on raised platforms without high outer walls
Water tank generally absent or outside complex

blocks.content: The Ramappa Temple (Ramalingeswara Temple) at Palampet, Mulugu district (now Telangana, historically in combined AP) received UNESCO World Heritage Site status in 2021. Within the current AP borders, the Amaravati Stupa is proposed for UNESCO status.

items: Match each Pancharama temple to its exact location (e.g., Amararama in Amaravati, Somarama in Bhimavaram, Kshararama in Palakollu).
Memorize recently added UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India, including Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple and Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas.
Note the architectural differences between Nagara, Dravidian, and Vesara temple styles.

blocks.content: The five Pancharamas are a group of five Shiva temples, each associated with a piece of the Shivalinga of Tarakasura, believed to have fallen in five locations in the Krishna-Godavari delta region. These are unique to Andhra Pradesh and are considered very sacred.

cells: Srisailam, Nandyal – also a Jyotirlinga (not a Pancharama, but major Shaiva site)
